chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

My father عليه السلام entrusted me with what was there. Then when death came to him, he said: “Call witnesses for me.” So I called four men from Quraysh for him, among whom was Nafi', the mawla of Abdullah ibn Umar.
Then he said: “Write: This is what Ya'qub bequeathed to his sons:”
“O my sons, surely Allah has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.”

And Muhammad ibn Ali bequeathed to Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and instructed him to shroud him in his cloak in which he used to perform the Friday salat (prayer), to place his turban upon him, to square his grave, to raise it by four fingers, and to loosen his worn garments from him at his burial.

Then he said to the witnesses: “You may depart; may Allah have mercy on you.” Then I said to him: “O my father, after they had left, this was not something that required witnesses to be called over it.” He said: “O my son, I disliked that you should be overcome and that it should be said, ‘He did not bequeath to him.’ So I wanted there to be a proof for you.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: made a bequest or testamentary instruction
key_terms.اسْتَوْدَعَنِي: entrusted me with something for safekeeping
key_terms.الْوَفَاةُ: death at the time of final departure from worldly life
key_terms.شُهُودًا: witnesses called to attest to the bequest

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام establish his bequest to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام before witnesses?
ai.summary: This narration describes how Imam Muhammad ibn Ali عليه السلام publicly established his bequest to Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام in the presence of witnesses at the time of death. It combines a Qur'anic testament with burial instructions and shows the importance of clear designation so that the proof of succession would be established.
